(2025). ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation. arXiv.
creator: Chenchen Zhang, Yuhang Li, Can Xu, Jiaheng Liu, Ao Liu, Changzhi Zhou, Ken Deng, Dengpeng Wu, Guanhua Huang, Kejiao Li, Qi Yi, Ruibin Xiong, Shihui Hu, Yue Zhang, Yuhao Jiang, Zenan Xu, Yuanxing Zhang, Wiggin Zhou, Chayse Zhou, Fengzong Lian (Tencent)
description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifacts. It contains 1,825 executable queries across nine domains and uses standardized execution with staged screenshots and checklist-guided multimodal judging to assess visual fidelity, interaction, and code quality.
name: ArtifactsBench
rai:annotatorDemographics: Human verification and evaluation involved experts, humans, annotators, and multiple front-end engineers with extensive front-end development experience; no further demographics are provided.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Checklist calibration used a 10% manually curated seed and achieved Cohen’s κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators. The paper also reports a double-blind 280-query, 6-model human evaluation study and uses pairwise consistency (Pair ACC), with automated evaluation reaching up to 90.95% agreement with human experts.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists are LLM-drafted and then human-refined for specificity and screenability; a 10% manually curated seed is used to anchor calibration, and humans verify rewritten prompts. Human validation is conducted in a double-blind setup with randomized sample order.
rai:dataBiases: The construction pipeline includes strict de-duplication and contamination control using MinHash, semantic similarity, normalized DOM/CSS/JS, and screenshot perceptual hashing. The paper also notes that fixed-interval screenshot evaluation may under-capture highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed through a multi-stage pipeline. Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots, then filtered, de-duplicated, rewritten by experts and LLMs with human verification, paired with checklists, validated for solvability, and standardized with a common execution harness.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source materials included candidate tasks from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and screenshot-based visual-to-query generation, before filtering and rewriting into executable benchmark queries.
rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Others
rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that fixed-interval screenshot evaluation may not fully capture highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions, such as multi-step user workflows or nuanced game physics. It also notes that the benchmark evaluates final artifacts from a single turn and does not assess iterative agentic refinement, debugging, or multi-turn development processes.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-collection processing included automated filtering of incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items; re-authoring or discarding flagged near-duplicates; expert and LLM prompt rewriting; post hoc difficulty calibration to a target 30%/40%/30% Easy/Medium/Hard split; lightweight classifier-based sub-category tagging with human spot-checks; and revision or removal of underspecified or brittle tasks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The pipeline applies automated filtering, two-stage de-duplication using MinHash and semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, plus screenshot perceptual hashing. Prompts are rewritten for clarity, completeness, and executability, and tasks are standardized through a deterministic execution harness with fixed resolution and seeds.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is presented as a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models and to support evaluation of visual fidelity and interactive integrity that affect real-world user experience.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses include evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifact generation, benchmarking visual code generation systems, diagnosing strengths and failure modes across task types and difficulty tiers, and providing a scalable alternative to manual human-preference evaluation for web and visual artifact generation.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Machine tools used in the dataset construction and annotation pipeline include LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots, LLM rewriting, a lightweight classifier for sub-category tagging, LLM-drafted checklists, Gemini-2.5-Pro for query classification, Hunyuan-Turbos for checklist generation, and multimodal referees Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B for automated judging.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The quality filtering prompt explicitly requires selecting privacy-free queries and avoiding sensitive personal information such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details.
